claim: Apple's full-year fiscal 2026 capex (~$14 billion) equals about 2.2% of the combined four-hyperscaler capex total (>$650 billion).
stance_target: Magnitude of Apple's AI-infrastructure underinvestment relative to hyperscalers
scope_conditions: fiscal/calendar 2026 guidance, sourced to Q1/Q2 2026 earnings calls
quoted_support: Apple's full-year capex equals about 2.2% of the hyperscaler total.

claim: Tim Cook stated on Apple's Q2 FY2026 earnings call that AI spending is 'incremental on top of the existing product roadmap, not a strategic pivot,' while acknowledging Apple is 'clearly investing more' in AI.
stance_target: Apple's AI posture is CHOSEN (deliberate capital discipline), per management's own framing
quoted_support: Tim Cook on the call said Apple is 'clearly investing more' in AI but described it as incremental on top of the existing product roadmap, not a strategic pivot.

claim: Microsoft's calendar 2026 capex guidance is roughly $190 billion, with about two-thirds directed to short-lived GPU/CPU compute assets, implying close to $125 billion of compute hardware spend alone; ~$25 billion of the raise is attributed to higher component prices, not incremental capacity.
stance_target: Composition and scale of hyperscaler AI capex
scope_conditions: calendar 2026, disclosed by CFO Amy Hood
quoted_support: Hood specified that roughly two-thirds of the capex is going to short-lived assets, primarily GPUs and CPUs... Roughly $25 billion of Microsoft's $190 billion 2026 plan is incremental cost from price, not incremental capacity.

claim: Amazon's trailing-twelve-month free cash flow fell 95% year over year to $1.2 billion, almost entirely due to AI capex, even as AWS grew 28% (a three-year-plus high).
stance_target: Real financial cost hyperscalers are bearing for the AI buildout
scope_conditions: trailing twelve months as of Q1 2026
quoted_support: Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow fell to $1.2 billion, a 95% decrease year over year, almost entirely because of AI investment.

claim: Apple's R&D spend rose 33% year over year to $11.42 billion in fiscal Q2 2026, faster than its 17% revenue growth, with on-device inference costs sitting inside the device bill-of-materials rather than as reported capex.
stance_target: Apple is investing in AI capability, just through a different balance-sheet line (R&D and device BOM) than hyperscaler capex
quoted_support: R&D rose 33% year over year to $11.42 billion in the quarter, faster than revenue growth. The architectural choice that explains the capex gap is on-device inference... The cost of that compute sits inside the device bill of materials, not on Apple's balance sheet as data center capex.

claim: The same quarter Apple announced Google Gemini would power next-generation Siri reasoning, its board authorized an additional $100 billion in stock buybacks — read as a signal Apple does not believe it needs to redeploy cash into AI infrastructure.
stance_target: Whether capital allocation behavior is consistent with a chosen, patient AI strategy
quoted_support: Earlier in the quarter Apple announced it would use Google's Gemini to power the next generation of Siri's reasoning capabilities... The board also authorized an additional $100 billion in stock buybacks, the clearest signal that Apple does not believe it needs to redeploy that cash into AI infrastructure.

claim: Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai said Alphabet is 'compute constrained in the near term,' justifying a capex raise to $180-190 billion for 2026, with CFO Anat Ashkenazi indicating 2027 capex will 'significantly increase' further.
stance_target: Demand-side justification for hyperscaler capex acceleration
quoted_support: We are compute constrained in the near term... She also told analysts the 2027 number will 'significantly increase' from the 2026 baseline.
